rows.practice: designs experiments and runs laboratory, field or computational work under risk assessment, collecting and analysing data to test hypotheses about living systems
rows.knowledge: the processes of life across all kingdoms, from molecular biology and cells to organisms, systems biology and ecosystems, with depth in a few sub-disciplines
rows.identity: a bioscientist in training who acts professionally and inclusively, respects legal and ethical duties to living resources and owns their personal and professional development

rows.practice: designs and optimises techniques largely alone, chooses and judges statistical and computational methods and devises solutions to unfamiliar biological problems with attention to controls and bias
rows.knowledge: a thorough and wide view of biology brought to bear on phenomena and problems, with an understanding that knowledge is fluid and new findings reshape it
rows.identity: a bioscientist who critically judges the ethics and social effects of biological advances and proposes how the field can meet present and future challenges such as sustainability

rows.practice: questions and combines wide literature to design new methods of investigation, then plans and discusses a significant research project with its ethics, hazards and sustainability
rows.knowledge: a systematic and broad command of current biological concepts, synthesised to solve complex and unfamiliar problems at the forefront of the field
rows.identity: an increasingly independent bioscience researcher who thinks critically and weighs the environmental effects and costs of their own investigations (ing's reading)

digest.definition: Biosciences is the study of life, a subject so wide and fast-growing that no one could cover it all, so degrees balance current specialisms with breadth
distinctiveFeatures: Biosciences is the study of life, a subject so wide and fast-growing that no one could cover it all, so degrees balance current specialisms with breadth
Graduates work across industry, government, NGOs and education, most of them outside research
The subject rests on objective observation, yet its history includes bias that courses are asked to confront
A broad, fast-moving field central to understanding life on Earth and often at the front line of global challenges
Its range runs from cell chemistry and evolution to physiology, populations, ecology and biotechnology
No course need span every sub-discipline; many valid paths exist within it
Often interdisciplinary, overlapping with biomedical science, chemistry, geography, the environmental sciences and data science
Courses mix experimental and theoretical work, often with fieldwork, and increasingly computational and simulated learning
Highly collaborative, with partnerships across education, employers and learned societies
Knowledge in it is often contested and provisional, and uncertainty is a key concept

themesInSubject.inThisSubject: Asks courses to confront the field's history of bias, credit diverse scientists, check materials for stereotypes and make practical work inclusive; graduates should understand EDI in the discipline and work inclusively in teams (D1, 1.10, 1.13 to 1.15)

Reaches laboratory, field and placement work at home and abroad: course teams must make the curriculum fully accessible by design, with individual adjustments and early contact with disability teams (D1, 1.16, 1.17)

Framed through the Sustainable Development Goals and practical lab and field sustainability, with particular weight on living resources and the three Rs in animal use; carried into the experimental design, challenges and professional conduct outcomes (D1, 1.7, 1.8, 1.18 to 1.20)
Employability is named a fundamental outcome: co-created enterprise education, work-integrated learning, placements, industry projects and careers fairs (D1, 1.21 to 1.23, 2.27, 2.28)

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: depth and breadth for a fast-growing subject
statements.paraphrase: Because the subject is vast and grows quickly in many directions, degrees need to turn out graduates with current specialist knowledge and skills and enough breadth to adjust as the field changes.

forPractitioner.text: Design for depth in a current specialism and enough breadth that graduates can adjust as the field moves; the text words this as a need, not with should or must.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: knowledge, skills and behaviours for society and careers
statements.paraphrase: Graduates should acquire subject knowledge, practical and transferable skills and behaviours that let them benefit society and the environment, connect biology to real problems and do well in biological and other careers.

forPractitioner.text: Plan the course so graduates should leave with disciplinary knowledge, practical and transferable skills and professional behaviours, able to connect biology to real-world problems and ready for careers inside and outside biology.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come away with subject knowledge, practical and transferable skills and ways of working that let you contribute to society and the environment, connect biology to real problems and do well in many kinds of career.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: a foundation from molecules to ecosystems
statements.paraphrase: Graduates should build a base of knowledge and understanding of processes and concepts across all the kingdoms of life, from the molecular basis of life up to systems biology and whole-ecosystem research.

forPractitioner.text: Give every graduate a grounding, at the right emphasis for the course, in processes and concepts across the kingdoms of life, from the molecular to systems and ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You should build a base of knowledge across living things, from the molecules life depends on to whole systems and ecosystems.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: No one can understand the whole subject in detail, so graduates should have a broad grasp of it and usually go deep in a few sub-disciplines, which may be reflected in a narrower degree title.

forPractitioner.text: Expect a broad understanding of the whole subject from every graduate, with depth in a smaller set of sub-disciplines; the specialism may justify a more specific award title.

forBeneficiary.text: You should understand the subject broadly, and you will usually go deeper into a few areas of it; your specialism may show in the name of your degree.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Degrees may draw on other disciplines, so designers may need to consult other subject statements such as those for biomedical sciences, chemistry, geography and the earth and environmental sciences; the focus should be on what those disciplines add to the study of living systems.

forPractitioner.text: Where the curriculum draws on other disciplines, consult their subject statements (for example biomedical sciences, chemistry, geography, earth and environmental sciences) and keep the focus on what each adds to the study of living systems.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Degrees will give students chances to examine, review and use sustainable strategies grounded in a sound review of current ideas, including technology, cost and scientific robustness, and to see sustainability as central to future ecosystems and populations.

forPractitioner.text: Build in activities where students examine and apply sustainable strategies, judged on technology, economic viability and scientific soundness, and connect sustainability to the subject's stake in future ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: inclusive, enquiry-led practical skills before the final project
statements.paraphrase: Graduates should gain practical skills in laboratory, field or computational settings; practical work should be inclusive and adaptable to individual needs, enquiry-led where possible, and well developed before the final-year project, which should not be the only place they are built.

forPractitioner.text: Teach practical skills throughout, in laboratory, field or computational settings, inclusively and in formats that suit individual needs; make the work enquiry-led and make sure students have substantial practice before any final-year capstone project.

forBeneficiary.text: You should build practical skills in the lab, in the field or on the computer throughout your course, in a way that suits your needs, and you should get plenty of practice before your final-year project.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: understanding EDI and its history in the discipline
statements.paraphrase: Degrees can be built so every student has an equal chance to succeed; graduates should also understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in the discipline and in society, including how history has shaped the field's thinking and cultures.

forPractitioner.text: Structure the course so all students have equivalent chances to succeed, and make sure graduates should grasp why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in the discipline and in society, and how history shaped the field.

forBeneficiary.text: You should understand why equality, diversity and inclusion matter in biology and in society, and how past events have shaped the way the field thinks and works.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Graduates need to see why communicating science to many audiences and formats matters, and courses can help them build those skills; graduates should be able to collect and judge information, draw out key messages and convey uncertainty well.

forPractitioner.text: Give students chances to practise science communication for varied audiences and formats; graduates should be able to gather and weigh information, synthesise key messages and communicate uncertainty effectively.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to gather and weigh up information, pull out the main messages and explain them, including what is still uncertain, to different audiences in different formats.

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree
Purposes and characteristics of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: fair, authentic, valid and inclusive assessment
statements.paraphrase: Assessment needs to be fair, authentic and valid; it should test how students apply knowledge and skills, transferable ones included, and inclusivity should be considered at every stage of designing and running it.

forPractitioner.text: Design assessments that are fair, authentic and valid, that test the application of knowledge and skills (transferable skills too), and that build in inclusivity from design through to delivery.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: inclusive course environments and shared responsibility
statements.paraphrase: The statement treats inclusion throughout; courses should create an open, respectful environment where everyone feels valued and knows their own part in inclusive practice, should actively raise awareness of equality, equity, diversity and inclusion, and should be reviewed regularly against institutional and government guidance.

forPractitioner.text: Design the course for openness and participation, where everyone feels respected and knows their role in inclusive practice; build awareness of equality, equity, diversity and inclusion into activities and discussions; review and update it regularly.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: confronting the history of bias in biology
statements.paraphrase: Courses should engage critically with how the subject has both fed and gained from social injustice, give a balanced history, encourage students to see how bias and culture shape science, examine present as well as past practice, draw on under-represented sources and check whether materials repeat stereotypes.

forPractitioner.text: Teach a balanced history of the field, including its part in social injustice; help students see how culture and bias shape what science is done and how; use diverse sources and case studies; and audit materials for hidden bias.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: diverse contributors, lived experience and ethical reflection
statements.paraphrase: Curricula should credit scientists of diverse backgrounds and the insight different cultures bring, let students explore topics that connect with their own experience, encourage them to weigh the good and harm of applying discoveries, including misuse that deepens inequality, and help produce culturally aware, ethical graduates.

forPractitioner.text: Credit discoveries by scientists of diverse backgrounds, offer topic choice that lets students draw on their own experience and culture, and build in reflection on the benefits, harms and possible misuse of biological knowledge.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: equitable access, inclusive design and reasonable adjustments
statements.paraphrase: Access should be equitable, in line with and beyond the Equality Act 2010, for physical and digital resources; entry should rest on potential; course teams must make sure all learning and assessment are equally accessible, by inclusive design and reasonable adjustments, and should let applicants talk to disability teams early.

forPractitioner.text: You must make learning and assessment equally accessible to every student, through inclusive design first and individual adjustments where needed; select on potential, cover digital as well as physical resources, and connect applicants with disability teams from the start.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: fully accessible curricula, fieldwork and placements
statements.paraphrase: Course teams must make curricula, teaching, assessment and practical work fully accessible and flexible; access to fieldwork, laboratory work and placements at home and abroad should be planned ahead, with individual adjustments where needed, so no characteristic bars a student from any part of the curriculum, and feedback should be used to remove barriers.

forPractitioner.text: You must design curricula, pedagogy, assessment and practicals to be fully accessible and flexible, plan access to fieldwork, labs and placements in advance, offer individual adjustments, and use feedback to remove barriers.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: sustainable practice; animal use and the three Rs
statements.paraphrase: Sustainability is central to the subject and wider than the environment; practical steps include cutting waste and plastics and weighing the impact of lab and field work; living resources need care, relevant law such as the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act should be upheld, and courses should strive to follow replacement, reduction and refinement in animal use.

forPractitioner.text: Model sustainable practice in labs and fieldwork, teach waste reduction and resource care, uphold the relevant animal welfare law and apply the three Rs (replacement, reduction, refinement) wherever animals are used.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Education for sustainable development builds curriculum structures and content that support sustainable development; understanding the UN Sustainable Development Goals is essential to it, and where fitting the goals should be woven through the whole curriculum.

forPractitioner.text: Treat ESD as a curriculum design task: where appropriate, integrate the Sustainable Development Goals across the curriculum rather than in one module.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Those including sustainable development in the subject should consult the QAA and Advance HE ESD guidance on teaching, competencies, outcomes and assessment; working with student representatives and sustainability teams may help.

forPractitioner.text: Use the ESD guidance published by QAA and Advance HE when writing sustainability teaching, outcomes and assessment, and involve student representatives and sustainability teams.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: employer links and co-created enterprise education
statements.paraphrase: Close links with employers in curriculum and assessment design will help employability; teaching on enterprise and entrepreneurship should be built jointly with employers, professional bodies and others and may cover planning, finance, sustainability, innovation and intellectual property, ideally through subject examples.

forPractitioner.text: Co-create enterprise and entrepreneurship education with employers, professional bodies and service users; topics may include project management, sustainability, innovation and intellectual property, taught through real subject examples.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Context and purposes of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: teamwork and responsibility for one's own development
statements.paraphrase: Alumni, entrepreneurs and practitioners may help shape authentic, reflective tasks; group work should foster teamwork, negotiation and leadership; students should own their personal and professional development, showing commitment to learning, self-improvement and helping others grow.

forPractitioner.text: Use group work to build teamwork, negotiation and leadership, invite alumni and practitioners into authentic tasks, and expect students to take charge of their own development.

forBeneficiary.text: You should take charge of your own personal and professional development, keep learning and improving, and help others develop too; group work should help you build teamwork, negotiation and leadership.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: progression through levels to the course outcomes
statements.paraphrase: Across an honours degree a student will move from one level to the next under the institution's rules after achieving each year's outcomes, building towards the course outcomes and the threshold skills, including credit for all learning and assessment such as practicals and field courses.

forPractitioner.text: Students will progress level by level under institutional rules, each year's outcomes building towards the course outcomes and the threshold subject-specific and transferable skills; credit covers practicals and field courses where they apply.

forBeneficiary.text: You will move up a level each year once you have met that year's learning outcomes, building towards the outcomes for the whole course, including passing practicals and field courses where your course has them.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: progression that recognises prior experience and transition
statements.paraphrase: Progression should take account of students' varied prior experience and the difficulty of transition, so all can aim high whatever their background, with support for personal and academic growth, not only for the subject content.

forPractitioner.text: Plan progression and transition support around students' varied backgrounds, and support academic and personal development as well as subject learning.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: core skills on joint and combined routes
statements.paraphrase: Students on combined, joint or major-minor routes will achieve the core subject-specific and generic skills of the subject and add others from their other subject; they may also explore where the two meet.

forPractitioner.text: Make sure joint, combined and major-minor students will achieve the core subject-specific and generic skills, adding others from the partner subject, with scope to study the overlap.

forBeneficiary.text: If you study the subject alongside another, you will still gain its core subject and general skills, add skills from your other subject, and may get to explore where the two overlap.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: increased critical thinking, research skills and independence in the extra year
statements.paraphrase: Integrated master's degrees run four years full-time (five in Scotland); in the extra year students are expected to show sharper critical thinking, evaluation and research skills and more independence, and the course usually offers an honours exit award.

forPractitioner.text: In the integrated master's year, expect students to show greater critical thinking, evaluation, research skill and independence than at honours; an honours degree is usually available as an exit award.

forBeneficiary.text: In the extra master's year you will be expected to show stronger critical thinking, judgement and research skills, and to work more independently.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Degree apprentices at Level 6 or 7 follow the usual rules for progression and the degree award, but must also pass the end-point assessment to receive the apprenticeship.

forPractitioner.text: Tell apprentices that the degree follows normal rules but the apprenticeship itself needs a pass in the end-point assessment.

forBeneficiary.text: If you are a degree apprentice, the usual rules apply to your degree, but you must also pass the end-point assessment to complete the apprenticeship.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: The field's pace keeps curricula varied; courses need to adapt to and anticipate advances in the subject and other fields and the needs of graduates and employers; providers may offer general or specialist routes and joint honours with other subjects.

forPractitioner.text: Keep the curriculum under review so it adapts to, and anticipates, advances and the needs of graduates and employers; the text words this as a need.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Courses may be run with further education partners, especially for foundation years, some biomedical courses and degree apprenticeships; such collaborations will have a clear programme with agreed outcomes, delivery modes, responsibilities and quality processes.

forPractitioner.text: When working with a further education partner, agree and write down the programme, outcomes, delivery, responsibilities and quality assurance.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Employability is a core aim, so engagement with employment sectors should be extensive and each course should set out a plain strategy for learning integrated with work; simulated work should reflect sector practice and be inclusive, and funding should be considered so placements are open to all.

forPractitioner.text: Write a work-integrated learning strategy, give students contact with employers, keep simulated work current with sector practice and accessible, and consider funding so all students can take placements.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Taught students may do their capstone project with an industrial partner; industry may help deliver apprenticeships; most courses should offer careers fairs; applied areas may set up industry steering groups; these build professional and entrepreneurial skills.

forPractitioner.text: Offer careers fairs, consider industry-partnered capstone projects and, in applied areas, an industry steering group for the curriculum.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: students as partners and the student voice
statements.paraphrase: Students should expect to be treated as partners in their courses, and their voice should count in development, delivery and review, through representatives, surveys, the union and review groups.

forPractitioner.text: Treat students as partners: give the student voice a real part in development, delivery and review, through representatives, surveys, the union and steering groups.

forBeneficiary.text: You should expect to be treated as a partner in your course: your views should shape how it is developed, taught and reviewed, through representatives, surveys and your students' union.

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.about: feedback sources for monitoring and review
statements.paraphrase: Monitoring and review should draw on feedback from current students, employers, placement providers and alumni to shape the curriculum, and from employers and apprentices for apprenticeships.

forPractitioner.text: Gather feedback from students, employers, placement hosts and alumni (and apprentices) for every review.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Student performance data and measures of the student experience should be combined with expert review, including external examiners' views.

forPractitioner.text: Read student performance and experience data together with external examiners' and other expert views.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

headingPath: Distinctive features of a Biosciences degree

statements.paraphrase: Externality is essential to UK quality assurance: providers will use external reviewers in periodic review to bring an outside view on changes and confirm that threshold standards are met and content suits the subject.

forPractitioner.text: Involve external reviewers in periodic review to test proposed changes, threshold standards and subject content.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: a foundation across the range of processes
statements.paraphrase: No single curriculum can cover everything equally, but students should build a grounding in a wide range of processes, from the molecular basis of life to systems and ecosystems, to suit the course's emphasis.

forPractitioner.text: Give every student a grounding across processes from the molecular to the ecosystem, weighted to the course's emphasis.

forBeneficiary.text: You should build a grounding in many biological processes, from molecules to whole ecosystems, weighted to what your course focuses on.

statements.about: contested knowledge, critical thinking and uncertainty
statements.paraphrase: Courses should help students see that some of what they learn is contested and provisional; students should be helped to question and think critically about their subject and to understand uncertainty as central to it, with its history in view.

forPractitioner.text: Teach that some knowledge is contested and provisional, support students to question it critically, treat uncertainty as a core idea and bring in the subject's history.

forBeneficiary.text: You should come to see that some of what you are taught is still debated or may change, and you should be supported to question it, think critically and treat uncertainty as a normal part of biology.

statements.about: a broad core curriculum, interdisciplinary in approach
statements.paraphrase: Courses generally include a broad core shaped by their emphasis, with in-depth study of selected topics; courses should take an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary approach to the processes of life from molecule to ecosystem.

forPractitioner.text: Build a broad core curriculum set by the course emphasis, with specialised depth in places, and teach it across disciplines from molecular to ecosystem scales.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Teaching moves students from structured, supported study to independent, self-directed work, with varied methods matched to outcomes; integrating topics is essential, and strategies should be enriching, stimulating, challenging, effective and enjoyable.

forPractitioner.text: Scaffold learning from supported to independent study, match methods to outcomes, integrate topics across the course and aim for teaching that is enriching, stimulating, challenging, effective and enjoyable.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Teaching strategies adapt to new thinking and technology in accessible, inclusive ways; all staff who teach, including demonstrators and visiting lecturers, should have access to professional development, and strategies should be student-centred and use varied, blended modes.

forPractitioner.text: Give everyone who teaches, demonstrators and visiting staff included, access to professional development, and use student-centred strategies across synchronous and asynchronous modes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment recognises achievement at threshold and higher levels through varied formative and summative tasks that grow with level and give useful feedback, including on digital literacy; assessments should be authentic and real-world and should allow reasonable adjustments.

forPractitioner.text: Use varied, progressive formative and summative assessment that separates threshold from higher achievement, make tasks authentic, and allow reasonable adjustments.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: assessment of and for learning, with feedback
statements.paraphrase: Assessment should serve learning as well as measure it, and come with useful feedback.

forPractitioner.text: Make each assessment both a measure of and a means of learning, with feedback attached.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessments should be valid, reliable and consistent and let students show mastery.

forPractitioner.text: Check each assessment is valid, reliable and consistent and lets students show mastery of the topic.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback should openly allow for accessibility and equality, diversity and inclusion.

forPractitioner.text: Build accessibility and EDI into assessment and feedback from the start.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: What students are told about assessment and feedback should be clear, open and easy to access.

forPractitioner.text: Publish clear, accessible, transparent information about every assessment and its feedback.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback should be planned so students and staff can manage their workloads.

forPractitioner.text: Plan assessment and feedback so workloads stay manageable for students and staff.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback should be part of the course and clearly linked to the learning outcomes.

forPractitioner.text: Make assessment integral to the course and map each task to learning outcomes.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback should let students confirm what they know and understand.

forPractitioner.text: Give students chances, through assessment and feedback, to confirm what they know and understand.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: Assessment and feedback should fit accreditation and approval requirements where these apply.

forPractitioner.text: Align assessment and feedback with accreditation and approval requirements where relevant.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.paraphrase: A suitable mix of formative and summative assessment should be provided, each supporting the other.

forPractitioner.text: Balance formative and summative assessment and link the two.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: unfamiliar problems and research skills at integrated master's level
statements.paraphrase: At integrated master's level the emphasis falls on students applying their knowledge to unfamiliar problems, and assessing the full range of research skills is treated as crucial in judging whether master's outcomes are met.

forPractitioner.text: Set unfamiliar problems in the master's year and assess the whole range of research skills when deciding whether master's outcomes are met.

forBeneficiary.text: At master's level you will be asked to use what you know on problems you have not met before, and your full range of research skills will be assessed.

statements.paraphrase: Feedback should be personal, understandable, empowering, manageable, developmental, timely and tied to the brief, with support to interpret it; it should allow reflection on development, and its nature and timing should be made clear in advance.

forPractitioner.text: Give feedback that is personal, timely, tied to the brief and developmental, offer help in reading it, and state in advance what feedback each task will get and when.

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.about: using Annex D to judge achievement above the threshold
statements.paraphrase: Most students will perform well above the minimum threshold; each provider sets what counts as evidence of higher achievement and should refer to Annex D, which describes the outcome classes for honours degrees at FHEQ Level 6 and FQHEIS Level 10.

forPractitioner.text: When deciding what evidence shows achievement above the threshold, refer to Annex D, the outcome classification descriptions for honours degrees (now in the 2024 Frameworks).

forBeneficiary.text: not-applicable: a duty on the course or provider; the student meets its effect, not a standard to reach

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, will remember the basics of the course's key concepts and phenomena and explain them in correct terms.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates recall the basics of the key concepts and phenomena and explain them using correct terms.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will remember the basics of the key ideas in your course and explain them using the right terms.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.about: applying comprehensive knowledge and enquiring further
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, uses thorough knowledge of concepts and phenomena to discuss and explain the essentials of the course, and shows enquiry that goes further.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates apply thorough knowledge to explain the essentials and show they have read and enquired beyond the course.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will use a thorough knowledge of biology to discuss the essentials of your course and show you have explored beyond it.

statements.about: key concepts and phenomena, explained with the right terms
statements.paraphrase: Will be able to explain, discuss and understand the main biological concepts and phenomena of the course with confidence, accuracy and detail, in the correct terminology.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will describe and discuss the course's key concepts and phenomena confidently, accurately and in detail, using correct terms.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to explain and discuss the main ideas and processes of your course clearly, accurately and in detail, using the right scientific terms.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, shows awareness of how broad the subject is.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show awareness of the subject's breadth.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will show that you know how broad the subject is.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.about: using breadth on phenomena and problems
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, brings a wide view of the subject to bear on biological phenomena, processes and problems.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates use their wide view of the subject on phenomena, processes and problems.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will use your wide view of the subject to make sense of biological processes and problems.

statements.about: awareness of the full range of the subject
statements.paraphrase: Will know the whole span of the subject, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will be aware of the subject's full span, from molecules and cells to organisms and ecosystems.

forBeneficiary.text: You will know how far the subject reaches, from molecules and cells to whole organisms and ecosystems.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.about: basic experimental design for routine problems
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, shows understanding of basic experimental design and uses methods on routine problems, with some attention to controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates understand basic design and solve routine problems, with some attention to controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will understand basic experimental design and use methods on routine problems, thinking a little about controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.about: devising and judging solutions to unfamiliar problems
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, creates and judges solutions to familiar and new problems with varied methods, alert to controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates devise and evaluate solutions to routine and unfamiliar problems by several methods, alert to controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will work out and judge solutions to new as well as familiar problems, using several methods and thinking about controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

statements.paraphrase: Will use knowledge of biological systems and methods to plan experiments and solve theoretical and practical problems, mindful of controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will design experiments and solve problems using their understanding of systems and methods, attending to controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to design experiments and solve problems using what you know about living systems and methods, thinking about controls, bias, ethics and sustainability.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, writes and follows risk assessments for practical work, with support, so it is done safely and reliably.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates write and follow risk assessments with support so practical work is safe and reliable.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will write and follow risk assessments for practical work, with support, so you work safely and reliably.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, writes and applies risk assessments without help so practical work is safe and reliable.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates write and apply risk assessments independently.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will write and apply your own risk assessments without help.

statements.paraphrase: Will explain, record and carry out safe ways of working that manage biological, chemical, laboratory and field risks, through informed risk assessment and practice.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will describe, record and follow safe practice for biological, chemical, lab and field risks, using informed risk assessments.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to explain, write down and follow safe ways of working with biological, chemical, lab and field risks, using proper risk assessments.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.about: competence in a range of techniques
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, shows competence across a wide set of suitable practical techniques for the course.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates show competence in a broad range of suitable lab, field or computational techniques.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will show you can use a wide range of practical techniques suited to your course.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, designs, refines and competently uses a wide set of techniques, largely on their own and efficiently.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates design and optimise techniques and use them competently, autonomously and efficiently.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will design and improve techniques as well as use them, working efficiently and largely on your own.

statements.paraphrase: Will choose and carry out suitable quantitative and qualitative techniques in the lab, field or on computer to solve course problems, understanding their theory and limits.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will select and use fitting lab, field or computational techniques, quantitative and qualitative, aware of their theoretical basis and limits.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to choose and use the right practical techniques in the lab, in the field or on a computer, knowing how they work and where they fall short.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, uses computational methods on familiar course concepts and reports the results in correct terms.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates apply computational tools to familiar concepts and report results in correct terms.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will use computer tools to look into familiar topics from your course and report what you find in the right terms.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, chooses and uses fitting computational methods on complex concepts and evaluates and reports the outcomes in correct terms.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates choose computational tools for complex concepts, then evaluate and report results in correct terms.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will choose the right computer tools for complex questions, judge the results and report them clearly.

statements.paraphrase: Will use suitable databases and computational methods to deepen understanding of biological processes.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will use suitable databases and computational tools to gain insight into biological processes.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use databases and computer tools to understand biological processes better.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.about: the evidence base in primary literature
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, shows knowledge of the evidence behind claims by finding primary papers and commenting on whether their methods, data and interpretation hold up.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates find primary papers and comment on how adequate their methods, data and interpretation are.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will find original research papers and comment on whether their methods, data and conclusions are sound.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, finds and picks suitable sources, primary papers included, and judges their methods, data and interpretation largely independently.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates select sources and appraise methods, data and interpretation with a high degree of independence.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will find and choose good sources yourself and judge their methods, data and conclusions largely on your own.

statements.paraphrase: Will work with the subject's literature to deepen insight.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will read and use the subject's literature to build insight.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to read and use research papers and other writing in the subject to deepen your understanding.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.about: planning and presenting supported independent work
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, plans, carries out and presents a piece of own work with data analysis or evaluation inside a supported structure, with some sign of time management, problem-solving and independence.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates plan, carry out and present their own work, analysing data within a supported framework and showing some time management and independence.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will plan, carry out and present your own piece of work, analysing data with support, and show some time management, problem-solving and independence.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, plans, carries out and presents own work very independently and competently, with critical data evaluation and strong time management and problem-solving.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates run their own project highly independently, evaluate data critically and manage time and problems well.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will plan, run and present your own project very independently, judge your data critically and manage your time and problems well.

statements.paraphrase: Will carry out independent, open-ended investigation in a project or research assignment, such as lab or field work, a literature review or gathering and judging data from varied sources.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will complete an independent, open-ended investigation: a lab or field project, a literature review or work with data from several sources.

forBeneficiary.text: You will complete an open-ended investigation of your own, such as a lab or field project, a literature review or a study of data from different sources.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, names and discusses uses of the subject in tackling present and future challenges, with some understanding of the scientists' role.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates identify and discuss applications to global challenges and show some grasp of the scientist's role.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will name and discuss ways biology helps with world problems and show some understanding of what biologists contribute.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, explains, proposes and critically assesses ways the subject and its scientists can help with present and future challenges.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates explain, propose and critique the subject's possible contributions to global challenges.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will explain, propose and critically judge how biology and biologists can help with world problems.

statements.about: the subject's part in innovation and sustainable solutions
statements.paraphrase: Will value how the subject has driven modern innovation and how its graduates can build sustainable answers to present and future challenges.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will appreciate the subject's role in modern innovation and their own potential to develop sustainable solutions.

forBeneficiary.text: You will understand how biology has shaped the modern world and how people trained in it can help solve today's and tomorrow's problems sustainably.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, names and explains how the subject relates to other fields relevant to the course.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates identify and explain links to other subjects relevant to the course.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will name and explain how your subject connects to others relevant to your course.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, explains and judges what the subject brings to interdisciplinary problems and how cross-disciplinary thinking helps solve scientific ones.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates evaluate the subject's part in interdisciplinary challenges and the value of interdisciplinary thinking.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will explain and judge what biology adds to problems that cross subjects, and how thinking across subjects helps solve scientific questions.

statements.paraphrase: Will see how the subject connects with other fields, scientific and otherwise, well enough to work effectively in mixed teams.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will recognise the subject's links with other disciplines and work effectively in multidisciplinary settings.

forBeneficiary.text: You will see how biology connects with other subjects, in and beyond science, and be able to work well with people from other fields.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.about: maths and statistics on familiar problems
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, uses mathematical and statistical methods to solve familiar problems or assess data.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates use mathematical and statistical methods on familiar problems or data.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will use maths and statistics to solve familiar problems or assess data.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, chooses, uses and judges suitable mathematical and statistical methods and tools to solve problems or assess data.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates select, use and evaluate suitable mathematical and statistical methods for problems and data.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will choose the right maths and statistics for a problem, use them well and judge whether they were the right choice.

statements.paraphrase: Will use mathematical and statistical ideas, methods and tools, such as handling equations, graphs and statistical analysis, to solve problems or assess data.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will deploy mathematical and statistical methods and tools, such as equations, graphs and statistics, to solve problems or evaluate data.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to use maths and statistics, such as equations, graphs and statistical tests, to solve problems and make sense of data.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, collects data accurately, chooses suitable analysis, interprets findings against hypotheses, considers next steps and prepares data for clear presentation.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates collect data accurately, pick suitable analyses, test hypotheses, consider next steps and present data clearly.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will collect data accurately, choose a suitable analysis, test your hypothesis, think about next steps and present your data clearly.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.about: independent data work in its field context
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, does all of this independently and accurately, with a thorough grasp of where the investigation sits in its field.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates handle data independently and accurately and understand the investigation's place in the field thoroughly.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will handle your data independently and accurately and understand fully where your investigation fits in the field.

statements.paraphrase: Will gather qualitative and quantitative data from course investigations and analyse and interpret it to test hypotheses, place and present findings and propose next steps.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will collect, analyse and interpret qualitative and quantitative data to test hypotheses, set findings in context, present them and suggest further work.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to collect and analyse data from your investigations, test hypotheses, put your findings in context, present them and suggest what to study next.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, takes part effectively in group work and makes clear contributions.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates take part effectively in teams and contribute clearly.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will take an effective part in group work and make a clear contribution.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, finds and uses good strategies for group work, adds clear value to team outputs and shows strong teamwork or leadership.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates use effective group strategies, add real value and show good teamwork or leadership.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will choose good ways of working as a group, add real value to the team's work and show strong teamwork or leadership.

statements.paraphrase: Will work with others successfully and inclusively, contributing positively and flexibly to what the team produces.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will collaborate successfully and inclusively in groups and contribute positively and flexibly to team outputs.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to work well and inclusively in a group, contributing positively and flexibly to what the team produces.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, conveys information, ideas, problems and solutions clearly, in speech or other forms.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates convey information, ideas, problems and solutions clearly, spoken or otherwise.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will explain information, ideas, problems and solutions clearly, in speech or in other ways.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, communicates information, ideas, problems and solutions to an accomplished standard, always fitted to the audience.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates communicate to an accomplished standard and consistently suit the audience.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will communicate in an accomplished way and always pitch it right for your audience.

statements.about: communication fitted to audience and purpose
statements.paraphrase: Will communicate well, choosing content, media and methods to suit audience, purpose and topic.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will communicate effectively, choosing content, media and methods for audience, purpose and subject.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to communicate well, choosing what to say and how to say it for your audience and purpose.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, describes some ethical issues and social effects of advances, with some recognition of the subject's history.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates describe some ethical issues and social effects, with some regard to history.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will describe some ethical issues and effects on society of new advances, with some sense of the subject's history.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, understands and judges ethical issues and social effects of advances, with some understanding of the subject's history.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates evaluate ethical issues and social effects, with some understanding of history.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will understand and weigh up ethical issues and effects on society of new advances, with some grasp of the subject's history.

statements.paraphrase: Will bring ethical awareness to work in the subject and understand its history and how its advances affect society.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will apply ethical awareness and appreciate the subject's history and the social effects of its advances.

forBeneficiary.text: You will be able to think ethically about work in biology and understand its history and how new discoveries affect society.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At minimum, knows that new findings can change current understanding and that much is not yet understood, and shows some ability to keep up.

forPractitioner.text: At threshold, graduates know findings can shift understanding and much remains unknown, and show some ability to keep current.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum, you will know that new findings can change what we think, that much is still not understood, and show you can keep up to some extent.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 1, excellent standard)
statements.about: folding new findings into existing understanding
statements.paraphrase: At the excellent level, clearly grasps that knowledge is fluid and can fold new findings into existing understanding.

forPractitioner.text: At the excellent level, graduates clearly see knowledge as fluid and integrate new findings into what they knew.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top level, you will clearly see that knowledge keeps moving and be able to build new findings into what you already understand.

statements.paraphrase: Will keep up with advances, sustainability included, and accept that knowledge shifts as new findings arrive.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will stay current with advances, including sustainability, and appreciate that knowledge changes with new findings.

forBeneficiary.text: You will keep up with new work in biology, including on sustainability, and accept that what we know changes as new findings appear.

statements.paraphrase: Will behave professionally, respecting legal, ethical and social duties and setting an example that gives a positive, sustainable and inclusive picture of the subject and its scientists.

forPractitioner.text: Graduates will act professionally with regard to legal, ethical and social duties, modelling practice that shows the subject in a positive, sustainable and inclusive light.

forBeneficiary.text: You will act professionally, respecting your legal, ethical and social duties and setting an example that shows biology and biologists in a positive, sustainable and inclusive light.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 2 (master's), threshold standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the master's threshold, achieves the row's outcomes with considerable support and guidance.

forPractitioner.text: At the master's threshold, graduates reach these outcomes with significant support and guidance.

forBeneficiary.text: As a minimum at master's level, you should reach these outcomes with a good deal of support and guidance.

statements.appliesTo: graduates of the subject (Table 2 (master's), excellent standard)
statements.paraphrase: At the master's excellent level, achieves the row's outcomes largely independently and autonomously.

forPractitioner.text: At the master's excellent level, graduates reach these outcomes with a high degree of independence and autonomy.

forBeneficiary.text: At the top master's level, you will reach these outcomes largely on your own.

statements.about: synthesising current concepts for complex problems
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to build, combine, synthesise and apply a systematic, broad understanding of relevant and current biological concepts to solve complex problems.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should develop and apply a systematic, broad grasp of current concepts to complex problems, integrating and synthesising across them.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to bring together a broad, systematic understanding of current biology and use it to solve complex problems.

statements.about: designing methods from wide reading, at the forefront
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to question and combine varied literature and other sources to design and develop methods of investigation and analysis, including at the forefront and beyond their own specialism.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should interrogate and combine diverse sources to design methods of investigation, including at the forefront and outside their specialism.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to question and combine many kinds of source to design your own methods of investigation, even at the cutting edge or outside your specialism.

statements.about: planning, conducting and discussing a significant research project
statements.paraphrase: Should be able to plan a project, weighing ethics, hazards, environmental effects, sustainability and cost where relevant; build advanced experimental and investigative skills for it; and discuss its background, context, methods, results and likely impact.

forPractitioner.text: Master's graduates should plan a significant research project (ethics, hazards, environment, sustainability, cost), develop advanced investigative skills for it and discuss its background, methods, results and impact.

forBeneficiary.text: You should be able to plan a substantial research project, thinking about ethics, hazards, environmental effects, sustainability and cost, build advanced practical skills for it, and discuss its background, methods, results and possible impact.
